title: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC flags show not open access, no full text, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no Zenodo/Dryad hits. The single NCBI 'pmc' link (PMC13587235) turned out to be a citing Frontiers in Oncology review, not this paper. One web search found no public data deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Patient counts come from the abstract only: 190 biomarker-evaluable patients (98 nivolumab, 92 placebo) out of 461 randomized in the CheckMate 77T trial (NCT04025879). I could not read the data availability statement (paywalled). I assume industry-sponsored (Bristol Myers Squibb) patient-level trial data is released only through a request process; I did not confirm that.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found (no accessions, no supplement in Europe PMC, no Zenodo/Dryad). I did not see the data statement, but patient-level data from a Bristol Myers Squibb clinical trial is normally shared only on request or by application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked: no files available. The obvious label, event-free survival, is time-to-event (censored) data, not a ready column.

a5_enough_rows.note: From the abstract only: 190 biomarker-evaluable patients, far under the ~400-row minimum even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Would be tiny if it existed.

a8_label_provenance.note: Event-free survival and pCR (pathologic complete response) are measured clinical outcomes, from the paper's description.

existing_models.name: The paper's own machine-learning event-free-survival model (CheckMate 77T biomarker analysis)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not visible: only the abstract was read; it lists the top predictors (ctDNA clearance, non-N2 disease, pCR, squamous histology, nivolumab arm).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrievable (paywalled); the abstract notes only 41% of randomized patients had evaluable biomarkers.

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable: with no public patient-level data and 190 patients, no model claim could be made or tested.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use tumour DNA in the blood, tumour mutations and pathology results to predict how long lung cancer patients stay event-free after surgery plus immunotherapy.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-patient circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) status before and after pre-surgery treatment, driver-gene mutations, histology, nodal stage and treatment arm; 190 patients according to the abstract (not verified).
plain_idea.predict: Event-free survival time and pathologic complete response (no viable tumour left at surgery), both recorded clinically in the CheckMate 77T trial.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Oncologists could decide which resectable lung cancer patients need perioperative nivolumab, but the data are not public and the cohort is too small to train a model.

ml_idea: Survival model of event-free survival from ctDNA dynamics and driver mutations; not feasible without public patient-level data, and n=190 is too small.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Search the paper's data availability statement for a public deposit; none was found in Europe PMC or repositories.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 and A5. No public patient-level data was found (paywalled, industry-sponsored trial, no accessions or supplement), and the abstract gives only 190 biomarker-evaluable patients.
